input:
are we locked into the current payment integration? We’re exploring alternatives.
The customer is concerned that they may be locked into the current payment integration and want the ability to switch to alternatives.

are tasks auto-assigned when letters go out to policyholders? We’re seeing delays.
Tasks are not being auto-assigned when letters are sent, causing delays.

we’re getting complaints again because letters to joint policyholders only show one name — it’s causing real friction with clients.
Letters to joint policyholders only display a single name, leading to client complaints.

I’m writing to request an update to the purchase order number on your invoice — this is causing reconciliation issues, and I need the invoice contact change reflected accurately in our records.
Customers cannot update the purchase order number on an invoice, leading to reconciliation issues.

Just need to know when we can expect the joint policyholder names to appear correctly in correspondence.
Joint policyholder names are not appearing correctly in correspondence.

And how do you handle document versioning? We’ve lost track of updates before.
The customer cannot reliably track document updates and needs version control.

It’s frustrating because bounced payments mean we’re reissuing them days later, which messes up our reserves and reporting.
Bounced payments force reissuing days later, disrupting reserves and reporting.

we’ve hit a snag with supplier payments again
The customer is encountering recurring issues when trying to make supplier payments.

We’re running into delays because the payee account verification step isn’t happening before the payment is sent out, which causes rework and client frustration.
The payee account verification step is not executed before the payment is sent, causing delays and rework.

We’re setting up a new team for claims handling and the permission setup is taking ages — each user needs dozens of boxes ticked manually and if we miss one, they get locked out.
The manual permission setup for new users is slow and error‑prone, causing lockouts.

Exactly — we need payee account verification to prevent delays. It’s impacting our reserves and supplier reporting too.
The lack of payee account verification causes payment delays, affecting reserves and supplier reporting.

when letters go out for policies with two named holders, the system only includes one name — and sometimes it’s the wrong one, which really messes up the joint policyholder names.
The system omits or misplaces the second joint policyholder name on outgoing letters.

We’ve had a recurring issue where payment detail checking isn’t possible before sending out funds, which leads to bounced payments and delays in reissuing them — it’s affecting our reserves and supplier relationships.
Customers cannot verify payment details before sending funds, causing bounced payments and the need to reissue them.

I’m having trouble pulling the latest supplier reports into the system — any idea what might be blocking it?
User cannot pull the latest supplier reports into the system.

we’ve got a repeat issue where letters sent to joint policyholders are only showing one name — it’s causing confusion and complaints from customers.
Letters sent to joint policyholders only display one name, leading to customer confusion and complaints.

I’m trying to reconcile the reserves for two recent claims at Elderfold Home, but the figures aren’t matching up with our internal spreadsheets.
The reserve figures for recent claims do not match the customer's internal spreadsheets.

we really need this sorted before the next claims batch goes out
The customer needs a current issue fixed before the next claims batch is processed.

That’s exactly what we need — especially with supplier integrations and reporting getting more complex each quarter.
The current product does not adequately support increasingly complex supplier integrations and reporting.

we need to copy access roles, not rebuild them from scratch every time
Users must manually recreate access roles for each new user instead of copying existing ones.

We’re seeing ... payee account verification isn’t done before payment dispatch.
Payee account verification is not completed before payments are dispatched, causing delays.

I need to reset my password for accessing the claims portal — can you guide me through that?
User cannot log in because they need to reset their password.

I’m trying to get a batch of claims documents uploaded and linked to the right reserves, but I’m not sure where the task queue sits in the interface.
The user cannot locate the task queue in the interface to upload and link a batch of claims documents.

can we generate letters automatically based on claim status? We’re drowning in manual correspondence.
Users have to manually create letters for each claim status, which is time‑consuming.

we’re blocked until this is sorted
The customer is blocked from moving forward until the issue is resolved.

We’re struggling because we can’t verify third-party payee bank details before sending payments — it forces us to reissue failed payments days later, which delays claims resolution for policyholders. Payee account verification would really help.
Customers cannot verify third‑party payee bank details before sending payments, leading to failed payments and delayed claim resolution.

Sure — every time we issue payments to third-party suppliers, we can’t validate their bank details ahead of time, which means payments bounce and we’re stuck reissuing days later.
Users cannot validate third-party supplier bank details before issuing payments, leading to bounced payments and delayed re‑issuance.

We’re seeing delays in claims payments because we can’t verify third-party bank details ahead of time — it’s causing reissues and unhappy policyholders. We really need payee account verification built into the workflow.
The platform cannot verify third‑party bank details before processing claims, causing payment delays and reissues.

We’ve been trying to automate those letters and hit a wall with the current defaults.
The customer cannot automate letters because the default settings are insufficient.

Can you walk me through how to attach documents to a claim? I keep missing a step.
The user cannot figure out how to attach documents to a claim and keeps missing a step.

we need to reduce those delays before next quarter’s audit
Delays in the platform need to be reduced before the next quarter’s audit.

when we generate letters for policies with two named holders, the system only pulls through one name, sometimes the wrong one.
The system only includes one named holder on generated letters for policies with two holders, often the wrong one.

we’re trying to streamline our claims handling and need help filtering tasks by due date.
Customers cannot filter claims tasks by due date in the platform.

Can you walk me through how to update the reserves section after a supplier payment has been confirmed?
The user does not know how to update the reserves section after confirming a supplier payment.

the permission setup is taking ages — each user ... they get locked out.
The permission setup for new claim handling teams is slow and error‑prone.

the bank info isn’t verified ahead of time, which causes delays...payment detail checking isn’t happening before funds go out, so we’re ...stuck reissuing failed payments days later
Bank information for third‑party payments is not verified before the payment is sent, causing delays and re‑issuing of failed payments.

we’re ... setting up a new claims ... ... permission setup duplication is slowing ... us by … … … ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ……………………………………………………
The permission setup process requires duplicate work, slowing down team onboarding.

We’re getting heat from policyholders because the system isn’t handling joint policyholder names correctly — it’s pulling in just one, and that’s triggering formal complaints.
The system only captures one name for joint policyholders, causing complaints.

Reports: click "Save", rage x3
The Save button on the Reports page is causing frustration and likely not functioning correctly.

they’re only pulling through one name, and it’s causing complaints.
Joint policyholder letters only include a single name instead of both policyholders.

We’re seeing a problem where letters sent to joint policyholders merge only one name — this synonym ‘multiple names on letters’ is critical because clients are complaining and it’s hurting our reputation.
Letters to joint policyholders only include one name instead of all joint holders.

The setup process is a pain because you can’t copy access roles — every new team member means manually selecting permissions one by one, and if you make a mistake, the handler gets locked out until it’s corrected.
Setting up new team members requires manually selecting each permission, and any mistake locks the handler out until it is fixed.

Got it. That’s a workaround, but we’re handling 200+ claims a week—manual edits aren’t scalable.
Manual edits to claim letters are not scalable for high claim volumes.

Hi Bryn, I’m having trouble uploading the policyholder documents for claim A13 — they keep failing validation.
Customers cannot upload policyholder documents because they repeatedly fail validation.

we’ve had two handlers locked out already this week just from missing a checkbox
Handlers are being locked out because a required checkbox is missing.

We’re stuck because we can’t copy access roles — every new handler needs permissions ticked individually, and if we slip up, they’re locked out of their tasks.
Users cannot copy access roles, forcing them to assign permissions individually and risking lockouts.

And what about roles? We’ve got adjusters, supervisors, and external auditors — can permissions be granular?
The customer needs more granular permission controls for different roles.

The PO we referenced doesn’t match what’s on your billing, and it’s blocking our payment cycle.
The purchase order referenced does not match the billing information, blocking the payment cycle.

We’re manually editing the letters before sending, but it’s time-consuming and prone to error with joint policyholder names.
Manually editing letters before sending is time‑consuming and leads to errors with joint policyholder names.

The permission setup duplication is a real bottleneck — every new user means manually selecting permissions, and one slip can lock someone out of their claims tasks.
Setting up permissions for new users requires manual selection and errors can lock users out.

Actually, we’ve noticed that the reporting module doesn’t always sync the latest tasks with our policyholders’ records.
The reporting module sometimes fails to sync the latest tasks with policyholder records.
